diagrams.title: Three Frameworks for Analyzing an Intrusion
diagrams.subtitle: From attack phase to technique, then to attribution: each framework answers a different question.

quiz.question: Which framework links adversary, victim, capability, and infrastructure?

nodes.label: Observed indicator
nodes.detail: Starting point: an alert, an IOC, or suspicious behavior collected by monitoring.
nodes.exam: An indicator alone does not tell the story of the intrusion: it must be placed in context.

nodes.label: Cyber Kill Chain
nodes.detail: Reconnaissance, weaponization, delivery, exploitation, installation, command and control, actions on objectives.
nodes.exam: The Kill Chain describes a phased progression; it does not catalog techniques.

nodes.label: MITRE ATT&CK
nodes.detail: Matrix of adversary tactics and techniques: Enterprise includes 14 tactics in its current version.
nodes.exam: The table in the 11 Strategies book shows 11: that is an older version.

nodes.label: Diamond Model
nodes.detail: Adversary, victim, capability, infrastructure. Enables pivoting from an indicator to the threat actor.
nodes.exam: Detailed structure not covered by the provided books: remember the four vertices.

nodes.label: Improved detection
nodes.detail: Use these frameworks to identify detection blind spots, guide CTI, and prepare exercises.
nodes.exam: ATT&CK is widely used to measure detection coverage and prioritize rules.
